layers.name: Chief Operating Officer · New York, NY
layers.text: Chief Operating Officer · New York, NY

layers.name: Your posting describes a company doubling in size while trying n
layers.text: Your posting describes a company doubling in size while trying not to double its complexity. That is the exact problem I have spent the last decade solving — most recently as COO of Meridian Logistics, where we grew from $38M to $121M with flat headcount.

layers.name: I noticed Northbay’s 10-K flags inventory turns as your top drag
layers.text: I noticed Northbay’s 10-K flags inventory turns as your top drag on margin. At Atlas Foods I led an S&OP rollout that freed $9.2M in working capital across four plants, and at Craft Retail I cut stockouts by 31% without adding a single planner. Operations should be boring in the best way — predictable, measured, quietly compounding.

layers.name: What drew me to your posting specifically was the line about “bu
layers.text: What drew me to your posting specifically was the line about “building the company our grandmothers could work at.” Culture at scale is an operations problem too. At Meridian, our eNPS went from +11 to +48 while we integrated a $60M acquisition — not because of perks, but because we fixed the processes that made people’s weeks miserable.

layers.name: I would welcome the chance to walk you through the routing-stack
layers.text: I would welcome the chance to walk you through the routing-stack rebuild in detail — it maps closely to your distribution expansion, and I suspect parts of it would transfer. Thank you for your time and consideration.
